expectations.text: Response identifies stock availability and backorder risk - not shipping time or print turnaround - as the real lead-time driver for apparel.
expectations.evidence: The delay on swag is usually stock, not shipping

expectations.text: Response requires written confirmation of current stock and lead time for the specific items and the specific sizes before any commitment.
expectations.evidence: Ask Ridgeline three things in writing: Is every size in stock now

expectations.text: Response treats the quoted 12-business-day ship time as meaningless without that stock confirmation.
expectations.evidence: a "12 business days" promise means little unless the stock exists

expectations.text: Response converts the requirement into a hard in-hand date rather than a ship date.
expectations.evidence: A hard in-hand date at the venue. Give them one date, not a ship date

expectations.text: Response rejects the proposed even 75/75/75/75 size split.
expectations.evidence: The even 75/75/75/75 split is the wrong shape

expectations.text: Response supplies a size distribution to sanity-check the order against, with unisex M the largest share at roughly 43% and unisex L next at roughly 29%.
expectations.evidence: Unisex M is about 43%, L about 29%

expectations.text: Response includes the remaining unisex shares at roughly S 13%, XL 10%, 2XL 3% and XS 1%, and separate women's-cut shares at roughly M 7%, S 6%, L 3%, XS 2%, XL 1% and 2XL under 1%.
expectations.evidence: Gives S 13% and XL 10% only; no 2XL 3%, XS 1% or women's-cut shares

expectations.text: Response states that the distribution stops at 2XL only because historical orders stopped at 2XL, and that real demand exists at 3XL to 5XL.
expectations.evidence: Says real demand exists up to 3XL–5XL but not that the table stops at 2XL because of historical orders

expectations.text: Response makes covering the 3XL-5XL range a supplier-selection criterion a supplier can fail, not a size-chart footnote.
expectations.evidence: a supplier that stops at 2XL fails the brief

expectations.text: Because the order is being placed late, response applies padding of up to 30% per size and style rather than a single flat uplift on the total.
expectations.evidence: The source allows up to 30% per size and style... pad modestly on M and L only

expectations.text: Response keeps the late-order padding (a stockout hedge) distinct from ordering early (a backorder hedge) and does not blend the two logics.
expectations.evidence: No distinction drawn between the stockout hedge and the backorder hedge

expectations.text: Response recommends collecting real sizes at registration as both more accurate than any distribution and better for inclusion.
expectations.evidence: Send a one-question size survey to the 300 registrants now. Real sizes beat any benchmark

expectations.text: Response asks whether the supplier will hold or ship to the venue, and whether the venue accepts shipments, from what date, at what receiving fee, and whether anything can be stored securely beforehand.
expectations.evidence: From what date does it accept deliveries? Is there a receiving fee? Can shirts be stored securely

expectations.text: Response instructs keeping every receipt, and states unopened surplus can be returned, raffled or carried into the next edition rather than written off.
expectations.evidence: Only asks 'can unopened shirts be returned?'; no receipts, raffle or next edition
